propositions: Event logs grow unbounded when no CI and no local cron exists to trigger compaction, because compact-on-close was removed to fix a 13m53s lock-hold P0 and no standing alternative trigger was implemented for library/CLI users.

The two-arm selection logic must pick both tickets lacking a snapshot with at least one foldable event (backfill) AND snapshotted tickets whose foldable count exceeds the threshold (recurrence), converging after a fold when the snapshot is created and live count drops below threshold.

The sweep must report compaction honestly by observing SNAPSHOT artifacts before and after rather than relying on return codes, because _compact_locked returns 0 for both successful folds and all three no-op branches.

Out-of-band compaction must work everywhere: a scheduled 6-hourly GitHub Actions workflow for CI-enabled repos, AND an operation-linked trigger after close that either folds a just-closed ticket if selected or spawns a detached worker via stamped advisory lock if a sweep-staleness clock indicates work is overdue.

The standalone compactor must stand aside when the store write lock is held by a foreground writer (to avoid competing with waited-on work), must not re-stamp its staleness clock on a stand-aside (to preserve correct recurrence), and must re-probe mid-run to yield to writers arriving during a long sweep.

The authorship ledger computation via git log --full-history is hoisted out of the store write lock (read-only, no lock needed) and amortized per sweep instead of per ticket using the existing full-history map, reducing lock-held time from hours to seconds even at large store scale.
